Reassigned from DPDP_ACT-0027, whose erasure test it does not meet. Specifies verified account recovery options (backup email, phone) as an account-security measure; a safeguard is stated, though it concerns account recovery rather than breach prevention.

Provides objection to automated decision-making and cessation of profiling with human review; cessation of profiling is not erasure of personal data on request, and the automated-decision category has no rule in v2.

Reassigned from DPDP_RUL-0175, whose one-year log retention test it does not meet. States server-side copies are deleted after 30 days and viewed messages disappear; an erasure mechanism exists, scoped to messages.
Describes maintaining the privacy policy and conducting impact assessments; no contractual security provisions between fiduciary and processors, and no other v2 test is met.

Reassigned from DPDP_RUL-0178, a breach-notification test it does not meet. Provides a clear, accessible means to exercise the correction right: Settings > Personal Information, editable fields listed, changes effective immediately.

Reassigned from DPDP_RUL-0178, a breach-notification test it does not meet. Provides two accessible means to exercise the correction right: direct profile editing in Settings and a support email route with corrections implemented within 10 business days.

Reassigned from DPDP_RUL-0178, a breach-notification test it does not meet. Provides accessible means to exercise the correction right: immediate profile editing in Settings and a support route for other data with corrections within 5 business days.

Provides a full erasure mechanism: permanent account deletion through a stated Settings path, with all associated personal data deleted or anonymized within 90 days of the request except where retention is legally required.
Provides permanent deletion of activity history within 24 hours through Activity Controls; the mechanism is real but scoped to activity data, and no legal-retention exception is stated.
States erasure within 90 days of a deletion request unless retention is required by law; weakened by retention for a reasonable period for business purposes and backups retained up to 12 months.
Provides permanent account deletion through a stated Settings path with all personal data (messages, media, contacts, metadata) permanently erased within 30 days and no recovery possible.
Provides automatic permanent deletion of messages on user-configurable timelines (1 day to 1 week) from both devices; an erasure mechanism scoped to chat messages rather than personal data generally.
Provides permanent deletion of Location History through a stated account-controls path, with pausing that stops collection immediately; the mechanism is scoped to location history.

Publishes a grievance route with a named Data Protection Officer and Grievance Redressal Officer, email and postal address, acknowledgement within 5 working days and substantive response within 30 days, inside the ninety-day period the test specifies.

Reassigned from DPDP_RUL-0208, a consent-functionality test it does not meet. Specifies a concrete security safeguard, mandatory two-factor authentication via Settings; a single user-side safeguard, with no platform-side safeguards described.

Reassigned from IT_ACT_2-0285, a government-blocking test it does not meet. Provides a Settings functionality to disable location sharing, after which location data is not collected; consent-withdrawal functionality for one data type, though IP-based approximate location may still be used.

Reassigned from IT_ACT_2-0310, a breach-notification test it does not meet. Specifies an organizational security safeguard, personnel responsible for oversight of security of the Business Services; no technical safeguards or breach-prevention specifics are stated.
